messages:
lia-finance: Quick heads-up — noticed a vendor notice: temporary surcharge on GPU capacity in eu-west-3 starting next billing cycle. Need a tight impact estimate for reserved commits and hosted pricing tiers. Who can run a back-of-envelope? :eyes:

raj-ops: I can do a quick pass. Do we know which instance families/queues are affected? eu-west-3 had majority A100 slots in Dedicated pools.

lia-finance: Vendor language: 'capacity surcharge on select accelerator SKUs (A100, H100) due to regional demand'. They quoted ~+18-22% on list price. No firm dates yet, listed as effective 2026-05-01.

matt-eng: If it's only list price, our reserved effective cost may already be partially hedged by committed discounts. But burst/spot and short-term buys will feel it. Quick ask: what's our current blended hourly GPU cost by region?

raj-ops: Pulled rough numbers in thread:
```
eu-west-3: A100 effective (post-commit) = $2.40/hr
us-west-2: A100 effective = $2.10/hr
blended hosted (global, token mix) = $0.000012 per token (approx)
```
If eu increases +20% -> A100 eu -> $2.88/hr. That bumps global blended hosted cost by ~8-12% depending on traffic split.

sophia-prod: Churn risk? If we need to pass any portion to customers, we'll be touching pricing/packaging. We should model small delta scenarios: absorb, partial pass, surcharge by region for enterprise.

nico-sales: For enterprise customers on committed Dedicated, we negotiated fixed pricing for the quarter. We can't pass this mid-term. For self-serve hosted customers, we could consider a packaging nudge (e.g., change bundle sizes) but prefer avoiding public price increases.

lia-finance: Action plan proposal: 1) finance to run SKU-level sensitivity across our product SKUs and packaging (3 scenarios: absorb, 50% pass, 100% pass). 2) infra to compute capacity scheduling options (shift workloads to lower-cost regions, capacity migration cost). 3) product to draft comms/option matrix for PMF-facing decisions. Target EOD for the first-pass numbers.

raj-ops: Quick notes on migration feasibility: shifting burst to us-west-2 possible but constrained by data residency & latency for EU customers. Also capacity is thin in us-west-2 for next 2 weeks; moving capacity might incur preemption costs. Rough migration cost estimate: ~$0.3/hr per active_gpu for cross-region transfer + cold-start overheads.

matt-eng: I can run a small sim overnight to show impact of routing policy (prefer cheaper region up to X ms latency). Will post dashboards.

lia-finance: Great. For the finance sensitivity please include: unit economics delta per 1M tokens for each SKU, tax/VAT implications in EU, and effect on gross margin % on hosted revenue.

ops-bot: automated report ready: committed utilization last 30d: eu-west-3 = 62% avg, us-west-2 = 54% avg. Peak ratio eu/us = 1.18.

nico-sales: Also add a sales impact scenario: if we restrict EU routing, enterprise that require EU-only may need Dedicated expansion, which could be an upsell but longer lead time. Worth mapping customers by region.

lia-finance: Good point. Sophia — can you get a list of top 10 customers by EU token volume and their constraints?

sophia-prod: On it. Will share a redacted list and suggested mitigation per customer (e.g., prepay credits, Dedicated offer, temporary SLA credit).

lia-finance: Final ask for first pass: a short slide (1-2) with: headline #s (blended unit cost delta for hosted), committed pool exposure, quick mitigation options + estimated margin impact. Deadline EOD.

raj-ops: Aiming for numbers by 1700 UTC. If anything looks catastrophic, we'll trigger an engineering/finance sync.

matt-eng: Posted initial sim results: routing policy that allows 30ms extra p95 latency can shift ~18% of tokens off eu-west-3 to us-west-2, lowering blended cost by ~6% but increases tail latency for some EU customers.

lia-finance: Thanks — please dump the raw numbers in this thread. We'll use those for the slide. :thumbsup:
